description: The low-pass of the later MS-20 revisions, the KORG35 circuit modelled as the nonlinear system it is, with the clipping diodes inside the resonance loop

params.text: Sets the cutoff, 20Hz to 20500Hz, ten octaves
Sets the resonance; it self-oscillates over the top fifteen per cent of its travel
Sets the level going in, ±24dB, unity in the middle; this is the level the nonlinearity works on, which makes it a resonance control as much as a gain one
Sets the output level, ±24dB, unity in the middle
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the fm jack before it moves the cutoff

inputs.text: The signal to filter, one filter per channel of a polyphonic cable
Moves the cutoff, one volt per octave, per channel of a polyphonic cable
Moves the cutoff through the fm attenuverter
Added to the res knob, ten volts for the whole knob

outputs.text: The low-pass, inverted as the circuit is, with a lamp showing its level

notes: turn drive down and the filter opens up and rings; turn it up and it clamps, thickens and goes flat. The resonant peak falls twelvefold between a 5mV input and a 5V one.
the channel count follows whichever of the audio and pitch jacks carries more, and each channel keeps its own filter state.
a polyphonic pitch jack with a mono audio jack therefore gives one signal through sixteen differently tuned filters.
with nothing in the audio jack, the top of the res knob gives an oscillator tracking one volt per octave, bounded by the diodes at about 2.5V peak.
menu: Oversampling — 1× (rawest, lightest), 2× (default), 4×, 8× or 16× (cleanest); the maker measured the worst alias at -40dB at 1× and -73dB at 2×

inputs.3:
0 to 10V · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
